source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: The demo mentions copying and pasting each submission into a brand-new chat, one at a time, as a way to avoid the context-bleeding problem from grading in one long conversation. Why does the lecture call this 'not terrifically repeatable'?

options.text: Because each new chat costs significantly more money to run than one long conversation
options.feedback: Cost is not the reason given. The concern raised is about the practicality of the manual process itself, not about price.

options.text: Because doing this by hand for well over a hundred submissions does not scale
options.feedback: The lecture notes the course has well over a hundred submissions at a time; manually starting a fresh chat and re-pasting the rubric for each one is possible but tedious enough that it is not a realistic routine at that scale.

options.text: Because a brand-new chat cannot be given the rubric at all
options.feedback: A new chat can absolutely be given the rubric by pasting it in again -- that is exactly the manual step being described. The limitation is the effort of doing it by hand, not an inability to include the rubric.

options.text: Because the course's learning platform does not allow more than one browser tab open at a time
options.feedback: This is not a constraint mentioned anywhere in the lecture. The repeatability problem is about manual effort at scale, not a platform restriction.
